timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

schema.name: Edit
schema.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

Welcome to HackerRank Orchestrate. Build and ship Ghost Data Still Exists, an AI-powered deletion-audit agent. Let's get started.

## Log check

`log.txt` didn't exist yet, so I created it in the repo root. It now holds a `SESSION START` entry and an entry for this turn. Each entry has exactly one `tool=Claude Code` line and one `model=claude-opus-5-5` line, both taken from the runtime. I re-read the file after writing to confirm this. I set `Language: py` because the starter has `code/main.py`; tell me if you plan to use something else. The October deadline isn't set in the repo, so time remaining is "not configured".

## The contract in my own words

**The task:** for each of the 518 requests in `dataset/deletion_requests.csv`, decide whether the person's data is really gone as of `audit_at`. If it isn't, write the plan to finish the job.

1. **Check the request is a deletion.** `request_text` can be in any language. If the person asked for access, a correction, an export or a marketing opt-out, the answer is `NOT_APPLICABLE` with `[]`, even if everything else looks like a deletion case.
2. **Find every identifier the person has had.** Combine the current values in `user_identities.csv` with past changes in `user_audit_log.csv`. The email on the request may be an old one. Old emails, phones and hashes can still show up in old systems.
3. **Work out the real state at `audit_at`.** `reported_status`, workflow results and activity outcomes are only claims. Check them against the evidence: SQL snapshots (including replicas), logs, JSON, PDFs, screenshots and text records. `system_activity.csv` covers everyone, so it includes unrelated people and decoys. The manifest doesn't say which case a file belongs to; you have to match on identifiers inside the file.
4. **Apply the policy.** For each record, `deletion_rules.csv` says delete, redact, anonymize, retain, or keep an account tombstone. A tombstone keeps `user_id` but must lose the name, email, phone, email hash and any other identifiers the rule lists.
5. **Decide the status.** `COMPLETE` only if every copy got the right treatment, every record that must be kept is still there, and no active sync, import or restore can bring the data back. Otherwise `INCOMPLETE`.
6. **Write the steps.**
   - `COMPLETE`: verification steps only, each citing evidence.
   - `INCOMPLETE`: findings that cite evidence, then remediation and verification steps with `evidence_id: ""`.

**Output:** `output.csv` at the repo root with the columns `case_id,deletion_status,steps_json`. Each step has exactly 7 fields, and you can only use the phases, operations and states the spec lists.

**Deliverables:**
- `code.zip`: the code, prompts, config, a README with run instructions, `evaluation/evaluation_report.md` and `evaluation/usage_report.md`
- `output.csv`
- `log.txt` as the chat transcript
- the AI interview

## Constraints that could cost points

**Format (one mistake can break a whole row):**
- Exactly 518 rows, sorted by `case_id`, with no missing or duplicate cases.
- `steps_json` must be valid JSON, quoted correctly in the CSV.
- `step_no` starts at 1 with no gaps.
- Only the listed operation and state pairs, e.g. `DELETE_RECORD`/`ABSENT`. No invented values.
- `NOT_APPLICABLE` must use exactly `[]`.

**Ordering (array order is scored):**
- Phases go FINDING, then REMEDIATION, then VERIFICATION.
- Within a phase, steps follow the order operations appear in the spec table, then `system_id`, then `resource_id`, both ascending.
- That table order means flows are disabled and restores blocked before records are deleted, redacted or anonymized.
- If you sort steps any other way, sequence accuracy drops even when every step is right.

**Evidence citation:**
- Findings and `COMPLETE` verifications must cite the specific `file_id`, `activity_id` or `audit_id` that proves them.
- Remediation steps and later verifications in `INCOMPLETE` cases must use `""`.
- Never cite anything captured after `audit_at`.

**Decision traps:**
- Trusting `reported_status` or a "success" result in the activity log.
- Matching only the current email, which misses records under old identifiers.
- Deleting records the policy says to keep. Over-deleting costs points just as under-deleting does.
- Removing a tombstone completely instead of redacting it, or leaving its email hash in place.
- Missing replica drift: the primary is clean but a regional or failover copy isn't.
- Missing active sync jobs or restorable backups that make a case `INCOMPLETE` even when every record looks clean.
- Letting evidence from after `audit_at` change the answer.
- Matching decoy records that belong to other users.
- Reporting incompletely: every violation and risk the evidence supports must be listed, each with its matching remediation and verification.

**Rule compliance:**
- Use only files under `dataset/`. No organizer data, hardcoded labels or shortcuts based on case families.
- Read secrets from environment variables only; nothing secret goes in the zip or the log.
- Runs should be deterministic.

**Missing deliverables:**
- `evaluation_report.md` needs status accuracy, step-level and field-level accuracy, sequence accuracy, at least 3 cases you created yourself, and a list of failures and fixes.
- `usage_report.md` needs providers, models, call counts, input and output tokens, average tokens per request, and total and per-request cost.
- `code.zip` must not contain `dataset/`, virtual environments or nested archives.

The 32 sample requests and their answers in `sample_output.csv` are the main local check for status, step and sequence accuracy. A natural next step is a script that scores our output against those samples on exactly these measures.

import csv,json,collections as C,os
rd=lambda f: list(csv.DictReader(open(f,encoding='utf-8',newline='')))
req=rd('deletion_requests.csv'); s=rd('sample_deletion_requests.csv'); so=rd('sample_output.csv')
ids=rd('user_identities.csv'); al=rd('user_audit_log.csv'); act=rd('system_activity.csv'); ev=rd('evidence_files.csv')
print("bytes check:", open('sample_deletion_requests.csv','rb').read()[:400][-200:])
print("reported_status", C.Counter(r['reported_status'] for r in req))
print("case id overlap sample/eval:", len({r['case_id'] for r in s}&{r['case_id'] for r in req}))
print("audit field_name", C.Counter(r['field_name'] for r in al))
print("event_type", C.Counter(r['event_type'] for r in act))
print("reported_result", C.Counter(r['reported_result'] for r in act))
print("src->tgt", C.Counter((r['source_system'],r['target_system']) for r in act).most_common(40))
print("resource prefixes", C.Counter(r['resource_id'].rsplit('_',1)[0] for r in act))
print("activity range", min(r['event_time'] for r in act), max(r['event_time'] for r in act))
# email resolution
cur={r['email'].lower():r['user_id'] for r in ids}
hist={}
for r in al:
  if r['field_name']=='email': hist[r['old_value'].lower()]=r['user_id']
for name,rows in (('eval',req),('sample',s)):
  c=C.Counter('current' if r['email'].lower() in cur else 'historical' if r['email'].lower() in hist else 'none' for r in rows)
  print(name,"email match",c)
print("dup emails in identities", len(ids)-len(cur))
# evidence inventory
print("ev by ext", C.Counter(os.path.splitext(r['file_path'])[1] for r in ev))
print("ev by dir", C.Counter(r['file_path'].split('/')[1] for r in ev))
print("ev origins", C.Counter(r['origin'] for r in ev))
disk=[os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dp,f)).replace('\\','/') for dp,_,fs in os.walk('evidence') for f in fs]
print("files on disk", len(disk), "unlisted", set(disk)-{r['file_path'] for r in ev}, "missing", {r['file_path'] for r in ev}-set(disk))
for r in ev: print(r['file_id'], r['file_path'], r['origin'], r['captured_at'], os.path.getsize(r['file_path']))
# sample outputs
print("sample status", C.Counter(r['deletion_status'] for r in so))
ops=C.Counter(); keys=set(); sysres=C.Counter(); evid=C.Counter()
for r in so:
  st=json.loads(r['steps_json'])
  for x in st:
    keys|=set(x); ops[(x['phase'],x['operation'],x['state'])]+=1; sysres[(x['system_id'],x['resource_id'].rsplit('_',1)[0])]+=1; evid[x['evidence_id'].rsplit('_',1)[0]]+=1
print("step keys", keys); 
for k,v in sorted(ops.items()): print(" ",k,v)
print("system/resource prefixes", sysres)
print("evidence prefixes", evid)
EOF

I inspected the dataset and wrote no code. This turn is appended to `log.txt`, with `tool=Claude Code` and `model=claude-opus-5-5` confirmed in the new entry.

## CSVs

| File | Rows | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| `deletion_requests.csv` | 518 | case_id, email, requested_at, reported_status, reported_at, audit_at, request_text |
| `sample_deletion_requests.csv` | 32 | same columns |
| `sample_output.csv` | 32 | case_id, deletion_status, steps_json |
| `user_identities.csv` | 850 | user_id, name, email, phone, email_hash, updated_at |
| `user_audit_log.csv` | 306 | audit_id, user_id, event_time, field_name, old_value, new_value |
| `system_activity.csv` | 4011 | activity_id, event_time, event_type, source_system, target_system, resource_id, reported_result, details |
| `deletion_rules.csv` | 15 | rule_id, data_category, condition, required_action |
| `evidence_files.csv` | 94 | file_id, file_path, origin, captured_at |
| `output.csv` | 0 | the 3 output columns (header only) |

- **Case IDs:** the eval cases run `case_33` to `case_550` and the samples run `case_01` to `case_32`, with no overlap. Sort numerically: in the eval file `case_33` comes before `case_100`, so a plain text sort would put them in the wrong order.
- **reported_status (eval):** 254 COMPLETE, 152 PARTIALLY_COMPLETE, 112 NOT_STARTED.
  - In the samples it's a poor guide: 11 of 17 claimed COMPLETE are actually INCOMPLETE.
  - 3 of 7 claimed NOT_STARTED are actually COMPLETE.
- **Sample outcomes:** 22 INCOMPLETE, 10 COMPLETE, and no NOT_APPLICABLE. So the samples give us nothing to test intent detection against.
- **Audit log fields:** only `email` (107), `email_hash` (107) and `phone` (92). Names never change.
- **Activity:**
  - 17 event types. The most common are DELETE_RECORD (890), UPDATE_RECORD (672) and SYNC_RECORD (447). Rare ones include RESTORE_BACKUP (1), CLASSIFY_REQUEST (10) and LINK_RESOURCE_IDENTITY (12).
  - Results: 2914 SUCCESS, 721 FAILED, 376 PARTIAL.
  - Events run from 2026-01-04 to 2026-10-01.

**Deletion rules:**

| Action | Categories |
|---|---|
| DELETE | USER_PROFILE, SECONDARY_IDENTIFIER, SEARCH_INDEX_ENTRY, CACHE_ENTRY, SUPPORT_ATTACHMENT (only if it belongs solely to the subject), USER_EXPORT, MARKETING_PROFILE |
| REDACT | SUPPORT_MESSAGE (shared context), EMAIL_DELIVERY_LOG (contains an email), ACCOUNT_TOMBSTONE (keep user_id only) |
| ANONYMIZE | ANALYTICS_PROFILE, PRODUCT_TELEMETRY (if still attributable) |
| RETAIN | SECURITY_AUDIT_LOG (within retention), LEGAL_HOLD_RECORD (hold active), BACKUP_ARCHIVE (restore can be blocked) |

## Evidence: 94 files, all present on disk, nothing unlisted

| Format | Count | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `.json` | 28 | snapshot bundles (`snapshots`), service exports (`service_exports`), connector configs and the security ledger (`records`), export jobs and manifest, analytics report |
| `.log` | 26 | key=value and JSON-line logs from many services and regions; the readback traces carry `lookup_key=<email>` and the field values |
| `.sql` | 24 | 11 inventory dumps with the same 10 tables, plus read, regional, reporting, failover and search-primary replicas; one header gives "topology" and "Captured at" |
| `.png` | 11 | admin consoles: account, analytics, backup restore, connectors, exports, marketing, object storage, search, security, support, tombstone |
| `.pdf` | 4 | account history, delivery correction, legal retention register, security retention extract |
| `.txt` | 1 | account handover note, 2026-10-01 |

Capture times run from 2026-01-29 to 2026-10-01. Several files are captured after some cases' `audit_at`, so we have to filter by time.

## How the data links together

1. **Request to user.** Match the request email against `user_identities.email` (418 eval cases) or `user_audit_log.old_value` where the field is email (100 cases). Every eval email resolves to exactly one user, and no email is shared between users.
2. **User to all identifiers.** Collect the current email, phone and hash plus every old and new value from the audit log for that user.
3. **Identifiers to resources.**
   - SQL, JSON and log records carry `resource_id` together with an email, phone, hash or `customer_reference`. `customer_reference` is probably the `user_id`; I haven't confirmed that yet.
   - Example: `customer_profiles(resource_id, customer_reference, full_name, email, phone, email_hash, account_status, …)`.
   - Flows come from `connector_subscriptions.enabled` and restores from `backup_restore_entries.restore_allowed`.
4. **Resource to system.** The ID prefix maps to a system in the samples:

   | Prefix | System |
   |---|---|
   | `account_` | account_service |
   | `search_` | search_service |
   | `analytics_` | analytics_platform |
   | `support_` | support_platform |
   | `export_` | export_service |
   | `data_flow_` | integration_service |
   | `backup_` | backup_service |
   | `audit_record_` | security_service |
   | `tombstone_` | identity_service |

5. **Resource to history.** `system_activity.resource_id` gives that resource's event timeline. The results are claims, so check them against evidence.
6. **Evidence to case.** Only through the contents. Use `captured_at` (and the snapshot time inside SQL files) at or before `audit_at` to pick the latest valid state.

## Output schema and step rules

- Columns are `case_id,deletion_status,steps_json`, with status `COMPLETE`, `INCOMPLETE` or `NOT_APPLICABLE` (`NOT_APPLICABLE` uses `[]`).
- Each step has exactly 7 keys: step_no, phase, system_id, resource_id, operation, state, evidence_id.
- The 15 allowed operations are fixed, in this canonical order:

| Phase | Operation | State |
|---|---|---|
| FINDING | REPORT_REMAINING_RECORD | PRESENT |
| FINDING | REPORT_EXPOSED_PII | PRESENT |
| FINDING | REPORT_ACTIVE_DATA_FLOW | ACTIVE |
| FINDING | REPORT_RESTORE_RISK | ACTIVE |
| REMEDIATION | DISABLE_DATA_FLOW | DISABLED |
| REMEDIATION | BLOCK_RESTORE | BLOCKED |
| REMEDIATION | DELETE_RECORD | ABSENT |
| REMEDIATION | REDACT_RECORD | REDACTED |
| REMEDIATION | ANONYMIZE_RECORD | ANONYMIZED |
| VERIFICATION | VERIFY_RECORD_ABSENT | ABSENT |
| VERIFICATION | VERIFY_RECORD_PRESENT | PRESENT |
| VERIFICATION | VERIFY_RECORD_REDACTED | REDACTED |
| VERIFICATION | VERIFY_RECORD_ANONYMIZED | ANONYMIZED |
| VERIFICATION | VERIFY_DATA_FLOW_DISABLED | DISABLED |
| VERIFICATION | VERIFY_RESTORE_BLOCKED | BLOCKED |

**Ordering:** sort steps by (position in the table above, system_id, resource_id), then number them from 1. All 32 samples follow this with no exceptions. Each phase occupies a contiguous block of the table, so the phase order comes for free.

**Evidence IDs:**
- In COMPLETE cases, every verification step cites evidence.
- In INCOMPLETE cases, findings cite evidence and all remediation and verification steps use `""`.
- Every citation in the samples is a `file_id` (`evidence_NN`). No activity or audit IDs are cited.

**Verification covers every relevant resource, not just the remediated ones.** For example, `case_11` verifies `account_4248` as ABSENT and `audit_record_9394` as PRESENT, even though neither appears in its findings.

## The 3 biggest technical challenges

1. **Rebuilding each resource's state as of `audit_at`.**
   - The same resource can appear in up to 94 files across six formats, plus replicas that disagree with each other.
   - For each resource we need the latest evidence captured at or before `audit_at`, and replica drift counts as a remaining copy.
   - Activity results like SUCCESS can be wrong, and syncs or restores can recreate a record after it was deleted.
2. **Deciding category and rule for each resource.**
   - Each resource needs a category and its condition evaluated: is this a shared support thread or one belonging only to the subject? Is the retention period current, the legal hold active, the restore blockable? Is the tombstone exposing an email hash?
   - That decides delete vs redact vs anonymize vs retain, plus the matching finding and verification.
   - Getting it wrong costs points in both directions: deleting too much and too little.
3. **Linking identities and pulling facts from PNGs and PDFs.**
   - Old emails, phones and hashes are spread across logs, and there are decoys belonging to other users.
   - Eleven screenshots and four PDFs need OCR or a vision model to extract resource IDs and field values reliably and repeatably.
   - Request-intent classification across languages is also untestable locally, since no sample is NOT_APPLICABLE. We'll need custom cases for it.

from datetime import datetime, timezone

import pytest

from data_loader import (
    DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR,
    SPECS,
    DatasetError,
    format_timestamp,
    load_dataset,
    load_table,
    parse_timestamp,
)

REQUEST_HEADER = "case_id,email,requested_at,reported_status,reported_at,audit_at,request_text\n"
GOOD_REQUEST = ("case_1,a@example.com,2026-01-01T00:00:00Z,COMPLETE,"
                "2026-01-02T00:00:00Z,2026-01-03T00:00:00Z,Please delete my account\n")


def write(tmp_path, filename, text):
    (tmp_path / filename).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


def kinds(table):
    return [issue.kind for issue in table.issues]


def test_parse_timestamp_normalizes_to_utc():
    assert parse_timestamp("2026-07-16T08:00:00Z") == datetime(2026, 7, 16, 8, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    assert parse_timestamp("2026-07-16T10:00:00+02:00") == datetime(2026, 7, 16, 8, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    assert format_timestamp(parse_timestamp("2026-07-16T10:00:00+02:00")) == "2026-07-16T08:00:00Z"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["", "2026-07-16", "2026-07-16T08:00:00", "yesterday"])
def test_parse_timestamp_rejects_naive_or_garbage(value):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        parse_timestamp(value)


def test_missing_file_raises(tmp_path):
    with pytest.raises(DatasetError, match="missing file"):
        load_table(SPECS["requests"], tmp_path)


def test_empty_file_raises(tmp_path):
    write(tmp_path, "deletion_requests.csv", "")
    with pytest.raises(DatasetError, match="empty"):
        load_table(SPECS["requests"], tmp_path)


def test_missing_required_column_raises(tmp_path):
    write(tmp_path, "deletion_requests.csv", "case_id,email\ncase_1,a@example.com\n")
    with pytest.raises(DatasetError, match="audit_at"):
        load_table(SPECS["requests"], tmp_path)


def test_duplicate_column_raises(tmp_path):
    write(tmp_path, "deletion_rules.csv",
          "rule_id,data_category,condition,required_action,rule_id\n")
    with pytest.raises(DatasetError, match="duplicate columns"):
        load_table(SPECS["rules"], tmp_path)


def test_bom_header_and_quoted_multiline_text_are_accepted(tmp_path):
    body = ('﻿' + REQUEST_HEADER +
            'case_1,a@example.com,2026-01-01T00:00:00Z,COMPLETE,2026-01-02T00:00:00Z,'
            '2026-01-03T00:00:00Z,"Bitte löschen,\nmein Konto"\n')
    write(tmp_path, "deletion_requests.csv", body)
    table = load_table(SPECS["requests"], tmp_path)
    assert table.issues == []
    assert table.rows[0]["request_text"] == "Bitte löschen,\nmein Konto"
    assert table.rows[0]["audit_at"] == datetime(2026, 1, 3, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def test_malformed_rows_are_skipped_and_reported(tmp_path):
    body = (REQUEST_HEADER + GOOD_REQUEST
            + "case_2,b@example.com,2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\n"                    # too few fields
            + GOOD_REQUEST.replace("case_1", "case_3").rstrip("\n") + ",extra\n"  # too many
            + GOOD_REQUEST.replace("case_1", "case_4").replace("2026-01-03T00:00:00Z", "not-a-date")
            + GOOD_REQUEST.replace("case_1", "case_5").replace("COMPLETE", "DONE")
            + GOOD_REQUEST.replace("case_1", " ")
            + "\n")                                                               # blank line ignored
    write(tmp_path, "deletion_requests.csv", body)
    table = load_table(SPECS["requests"], tmp_path)
    assert [row["case_id"] for row in table.rows] == ["case_1"]
    assert kinds(table) == ["field_count", "field_count", "bad_timestamp", "bad_enum", "missing_id"]
    assert [issue.line for issue in table.issues] == [3, 4, 5, 6, 7]


def test_duplicate_ids_keep_first_row(tmp_path):
    write(tmp_path, "deletion_requests.csv",
          REQUEST_HEADER + GOOD_REQUEST + GOOD_REQUEST.replace("a@example.com", "b@example.com"))
    table = load_table(SPECS["requests"], tmp_path)
    assert [row["email"] for row in table.rows] == ["a@example.com"]
    assert kinds(table) == ["duplicate_id"]
    assert "first seen on line 2" in table.issues[0].detail


def test_invalid_steps_json_is_reported(tmp_path):

          "user_id,name,email,phone,email_hash,updated_at\n"
          "user_1,A,a@example.com,+1,h,2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\n")
    write(tmp_path, "user_audit_log.csv",
          "audit_id,user_id,event_time,field_name,old_value,new_value\n"
          "audit_1,user_1,2026-01-01T00:00:00Z,email,old@example.com,a@example.com\n"

The data loader is built and all 15 tests pass. The real dataset loads with no issues, and no case classification is in place yet.

**What it does** ([code/data_loader.py](code/data_loader.py)):
- **Schemas:** each of the 9 CSVs has a definition giving its required columns, ID column, timestamp columns, allowed values for enum columns, and JSON columns. Columns not in the definition are kept, not rejected.
- **Fatal errors:** a missing file, an empty file, a missing required column or a repeated column header stops loading with an error.
- **Bad rows:** these are skipped and logged with their CSV line number. That covers rows with the wrong number of fields, a blank ID, a duplicate ID (the first one is kept), an unreadable timestamp, an unknown enum value, or invalid JSON in `steps_json`.
- **Timestamps:** everything is converted to UTC, so comparisons against `audit_at` are always consistent. A timestamp with no timezone is treated as an error.
- **Cross-file ID checks:**
  - audit-log `user_id`s that don't exist in `user_identities.csv`
  - sample requests with no sample answer, and answers with no request
  - case IDs that appear in both the eval and sample files
  - manifest entries whose evidence file is missing on disk
  - files on disk that aren't in the manifest
- **Encoding:** files are read as UTF-8. A leading byte-order mark is tolerated, and quoted text that spans multiple lines comes through intact.
- **Command line:** `python code/data_loader.py [dataset_dir]` prints row counts and every issue found. It exits with 0 if clean, 1 if there are issues, or 2 on a fatal error.

**Results on the real data:** row counts are 518 / 32 / 32 / 850 / 306 / 4011 / 15 / 94 / 0, with no issues.

**Tests** ([code/tests/test_data_loader.py](code/tests/test_data_loader.py)) cover:
- timestamp parsing, including rejected formats
- missing, empty or misnamed files and columns
- a mixed set of bad rows, checking the issue types and line numbers
- duplicate IDs and invalid JSON
- the cross-file checks
- loading the real dataset cleanly

Run them with `python -m pytest code/tests`.

One test failed on the first run because of the test itself, not the loader. On Windows, writing the test file converted `\n` to `\r\n`. I changed the test to write line endings exactly as given.

I also allowed `name` as a value in the audit log's `field_name` column, even though the current data only uses email, email_hash and phone. This turn is appended to `log.txt`.

from datetime import datetime, timezone

import pytest

from data_loader import DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR, load_dataset
from identity import build_identity_index, normalize

IDENTITY_HEADER = "user_id,name,email,phone,email_hash,updated_at\n"
AUDIT_HEADER = "audit_id,user_id,event_time,field_name,old_value,new_value\n"


def ts(text):
    return datetime.fromisoformat(text).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def build(tmp_path, identities, audit=""):
    (tmp_path / "user_identities.csv").write_text(IDENTITY_HEADER + identities,
                                                  encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    (tmp_path / "user_audit_log.csv").write_text(AUDIT_HEADER + audit,
                                                 encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    return build_identity_index(load_dataset(tmp_path, names=("identities", "audit_log")))


def test_normalize():
    assert normalize("email", "  Ana.Silva@Example.COM ") == "ana.silva@example.com"
    assert normalize("phone", "+33 6 24-34.80 16") == "+33624348016"
    assert normalize("name", "  Mateo   Ríos ") == "mateo ríos"


def test_changed_email_yields_both_values_with_periods(tmp_path):
    index = build(
        tmp_path,
        "user_1,Ana Silva,ana.new@example.com,+1 555 0100,hnew,2026-05-01T00:00:00Z\n",
        "audit_1,user_1,2026-02-01T00:00:00Z,email,ana.old@example.com,ana.mid@example.com\n"
        "audit_2,user_1,2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,email,ana.mid@example.com,ana.new@example.com\n"
        "audit_3,user_1,2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,email_hash,hmid,hnew\n"
        "audit_4,user_1,2026-02-01T00:00:00Z,email_hash,hold,hmid\n",
    )
    user = index["user_1"]
    assert user.values("email") == ["ana.old@example.com", "ana.mid@example.com",
                                    "ana.new@example.com"]
    assert user.values("email_hash") == ["hold", "hmid", "hnew"]
    assert user.current("email") == "ana.new@example.com"
    emails = [p for p in user.periods if p.field == "email"]
    assert [(p.valid_from, p.valid_to) for p in emails] == [
        (None, ts("2026-02-01T00:00:00")),
        (ts("2026-02-01T00:00:00"), ts("2026-04-01T00:00:00")),
        (ts("2026-04-01T00:00:00"), None),
    ]
    assert emails[0].sources == ("audit_1",)
    assert emails[2].sources == ("audit_2", "user_identities")
    assert user.held_at("email", ts("2026-03-01T00:00:00")) == ["ana.mid@example.com"]
    # A request made with a historical email still resolves, case-insensitively.
    resolution = index.resolve("email", "ANA.OLD@example.com", ts("2026-06-01T00:00:00"))

from datetime import datetime, timezone

import pytest

from data_loader import DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR, load_dataset
from identity import build_identity_index, normalize

IDENTITY_HEADER = "user_id,name,email,phone,email_hash,updated_at\n"
AUDIT_HEADER = "audit_id,user_id,event_time,field_name,old_value,new_value\n"


def ts(text):
    return datetime.fromisoformat(text).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def build(tmp_path, identities, audit=""):
    (tmp_path / "user_identities.csv").write_text(IDENTITY_HEADER + identities,
                                                  encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    (tmp_path / "user_audit_log.csv").write_text(AUDIT_HEADER + audit,
                                                 encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    return build_identity_index(load_dataset(tmp_path, names=("identities", "audit_log")))


def test_normalize():
    assert normalize("email", "  Ana.Silva@Example.COM ") == "ana.silva@example.com"
    assert normalize("phone", "+33 6 24-34.80 16") == "+33624348016"
    assert normalize("name", "  Mateo   Ríos ") == "mateo ríos"


def test_changed_email_yields_both_values_with_periods(tmp_path):
    index = build(
        tmp_path,
        "user_1,Ana Silva,ana.new@example.com,+1 555 0100,hnew,2026-05-01T00:00:00Z\n",
        "audit_1,user_1,2026-02-01T00:00:00Z,email,ana.old@example.com,ana.mid@example.com\n"
        "audit_2,user_1,2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,email,ana.mid@example.com,ana.new@example.com\n"
        "audit_3,user_1,2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,email_hash,hmid,hnew\n"
        "audit_4,user_1,2026-02-01T00:00:00Z,email_hash,hold,hmid\n",
    )
    user = index["user_1"]
    assert user.values("email") == ["ana.old@example.com", "ana.mid@example.com",
                                    "ana.new@example.com"]
    assert user.values("email_hash") == ["hold", "hmid", "hnew"]
    assert user.current("email") == "ana.new@example.com"
    emails = [p for p in user.periods if p.field == "email"]
    assert [(p.valid_from, p.valid_to) for p in emails] == [
        (None, ts("2026-02-01T00:00:00")),
        (ts("2026-02-01T00:00:00"), ts("2026-04-01T00:00:00")),
        (ts("2026-04-01T00:00:00"), None),
    ]
    assert emails[0].sources == ("audit_1",)
    assert emails[2].sources == ("audit_2", "user_identities")
    assert user.held_at("email", ts("2026-03-01T00:00:00")) == ["ana.mid@example.com"]
    # A request made with a historical email still resolves, case-insensitively.
    resolution = index.resolve("email", "ANA.OLD@example.com", ts("2026-06-01T00:00:00"))
    assert (resolution.user_id, resolution.reason) == ("user_1", "sole_holder")
    assert index.issues == []


def test_missing_history_uses_snapshot_only(tmp_path):
    index = build(tmp_path, "user_1,Li Wei,li@example.com,+86 138 0000 0000,h1,"
                            "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\n")
    user = index["user_1"]
    assert {p.field: p.value for p in user.periods} == {
        "email": "li@example.com", "phone": "+86 138 0000 0000",
        "email_hash": "h1", "name": "Li Wei"}
    assert all(p.valid_from is None and p.valid_to is None for p in user.periods)
    assert all(p.sources == ("user_identities",) for p in user.periods)
    assert index.resolve("phone", "+86 13800000000").user_id == "user_1"


def test_reused_email_resolves_by_time(tmp_path):
    index = build(
        tmp_path,
        "user_1,Sam Lee,sam.new@example.com,+1 1,h1,2026-05-01T00:00:00Z\n"
        "user_2,Sam Lee,shared@example.com,+1 2,h2,2026-05-01T00:00:00Z\n",
        "audit_1,user_1,2026-02-01T00:00:00Z,email,shared@example.com,sam.new@example.com\n"
        "audit_2,user_2,2026-04-01T00:00:00Z,email,other@example.com,shared@example.com\n",
    )
    assert index.owners("email", "shared@example.com") == {"user_1", "user_2"}
    before = index.resolve("email", "shared@example.com", ts("2026-01-15T00:00:00"))
    gap = index.resolve("email", "shared@example.com", ts("2026-03-01T00:00:00"))
    after = index.resolve("email", "shared@example.com", ts("2026-06-01T00:00:00"))
    assert (before.user_id, before.reason) == ("user_1", "held_at")
    assert (gap.user_id, gap.reason) == ("user_1", "held_before")
    assert (after.user_id, after.reason) == ("user_2", "held_at")
    assert after.ambiguous
    undated = index.resolve("email", "shared@example.com")
    assert (undated.user_id, undated.reason) == (None, "ambiguous")
    # Shared names are indexed but cannot be used to resolve a subject.
    assert len(index.lookup("name", "sam lee")) == 2
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        index.resolve("name", "Sam Lee")


def test_unrelated_users_do_not_leak_identifiers(tmp_path):
    index = build(
        tmp_path,
        "user_1,Ana Silva,ana@example.com,+1 1,h1,2026-05-01T00:00:00Z\n"
        "user_2,Ben Okafor,ben@example.com,+1 2,h2,2026-05-01T00:00:00Z\n",
        "audit_1,user_2,2026-02-01T00:00:00Z,email,ben.old@example.com,ben@example.com\n",
    )
    assert index["user_1"].normalized_values() == {"ana@example.com", "+11", "h1", "ana silva"}
    assert "ben.old@example.com" not in index["user_1"].normalized_values()
    assert index.resolve("email", "ben.old@example.com").user_id == "user_2"
    decoy = index.resolve("email", "ana.silva@example.com")
    assert (decoy.user_id, decoy.candidates, decoy.reason) == (None, (), "no_match")


def test_inconsistent_history_is_kept_and_reported(tmp_path):
    index = build(
        tmp_path,
        "user_1,Ana Silva,ana.snapshot@example.com,+1 1,h1,2026-05-01T00:00:00Z\n",
        "audit_1,user_1,2026-02-01T00:00:00Z,email,a@example.com,b@example.com\n"
        "audit_2,user_1,2026-03-01T00:00:00Z,email,c@example.com,d@example.com\n",
    )
    assert set(index["user_1"].values("email")) == {
        "a@example.com", "b@example.com", "c@example.com", "d@example.com",
        "ana.snapshot@example.com"}
    assert index["user_1"].current("email") == "ana.snapshot@example.com"
    assert len(index.issues) == 2


@pytest.mark.skipif(not (DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR / "user_audit_log.csv").is_file(),
                    reason="participant dataset not present")
def test_real_dataset_resolves_every_request_email():
    dataset = load_dataset(names=("identities", "audit_log", "requests", "sample_requests"))
    index = build_identity_index(dataset)
    assert index.issues == []
    for table in ("requests", "sample_requests"):
        for row in dataset[table].rows:
            resolution = index.resolve("email", row["email"], row["requested_at"])
            assert resolution.user_id is not None, row["case_id"]
            assert not resolution.ambiguous, row["case_id"]

Identity resolution is working: all 518 eval request emails and all 32 sample emails resolve to exactly one user. 418 match a current email and 100 match a historical one. All 22 tests pass (7 new, 15 existing).

**What it returns** ([code/identity.py](code/identity.py)): for each user and each field (email, phone, email_hash, name), a list of periods, each giving a value and when it was valid.
- **Validity rules:** a period starts when its value was set and ends when it was replaced. The value before the first recorded change has an unknown start, and the latest value has no end.
- **Sources:** each period cites the `audit_id`s that start and end it, or `user_identities` for the current snapshot.
- **Example,** `user_10`'s email history:
  - `nadia.ionescu@…` from an unknown start until 2025-12-13 (`audit_121`)
  - `nadia.petrescu@…` from 2025-12-13 until 2026-04-12 (`audit_121`, `audit_238`)
  - `n.petrescu@…` from 2026-04-12 to now (`audit_238` and the snapshot)
- **Helpers:** `values()`, `current()`, `held_at(field, time)` and `normalized_values()`. The last one returns the set of identifiers used to match evidence later.
- **Matching:** emails and hashes are compared case-insensitively. Phones are compared on `+` and digits only, so differently formatted numbers match. Names ignore case and extra whitespace.

**Resolving a value to a user** (`resolve(field, value, at)`): it tries these in order and records which rule matched:
1. The user who held the value at the given time.
2. Otherwise, the user who held it most recently before that time.
3. Otherwise, the only user who ever held it.
4. Otherwise it returns no user, with all candidates listed (or "no match").

Names can't be used to resolve a person: three names are shared by two users each, so `resolve` rejects them. You can still look names up.

**Bad history:** if an audit chain has gaps, or its last value disagrees with the snapshot, every value it mentions is still kept and the problem is logged. The real data has none of these.

**Tests** ([code/tests/test_identity.py](code/tests/test_identity.py)) cover:
- an email changed twice, with its periods and resolution by an old address in different case
- a user with no history, where only the snapshot is used
- one email held by two users at different times, resolved by time (before, in the gap, after, and with no time given), plus the shared-name rejection
- unrelated users: no identifiers leak between them, and a decoy address returns no match
- broken audit chains
- every real request email resolving to exactly one user

**Not included yet:**
- The resolver doesn't generate an email hash for an address that never had one recorded. Every email in the dataset has its hash recorded, and hash = SHA-256 of the lowercased email if we need to compute one later.
- Nothing classifies or decides cases yet.

"""Deterministic local OCR for evidence screenshots, cached by file content.

RapidOCR (ONNX runtime, CPU) is slow on full-size screenshots (~30 s each),
so results are cached as JSON under <repo>/.cache/ocr/<sha256>.json. The cache
key is the image's content hash, so a changed image is always re-read.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR = REPO_ROOT / ".cache" / "ocr"
CACHE_VERSION = 1

_engine = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OcrBox:
    text: str
    x0: float
    y0: float
    x1: float
    y1: float
    confidence: float

    @property
    def y_center(self) -> float:
        return (self.y0 + self.y1) / 2


def _get_engine():
    global _engine
    if _engine is None:
        try:
            from rapidocr_onnxruntime import RapidOCR
        except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - depends on environment
            raise RuntimeError(
                "rapidocr_onnxruntime is required to read image evidence; "
                "install it with: pip install -r requirements.txt") from exc
        _engine = RapidOCR()
    return _engine


def ocr_image(path: Path | str, cache_dir: Path | str | None = DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR) -> list[OcrBox]:
    path = Path(path)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    cache_file = Path(cache_dir) / f"{digest}.json" if cache_dir else None
    if cache_file and cache_file.is_file():
        cached = json.loads(cache_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if cached.get("version") == CACHE_VERSION:
            return [OcrBox(**box) for box in cached["boxes"]]

    result, _ = _get_engine()(str(path))
    boxes = []
    for points, text, confidence in result or ():
        xs = [p[0] for p in points]
        ys = [p[1] for p in points]
        boxes.append(OcrBox(text, float(min(xs)), float(min(ys)), float(max(xs)),
                            float(max(ys)), float(confidence)))
    boxes.sort(key=lambda b: (round(b.y_center), b.x0))

    if cache_file:
        cache_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        payload = {"version": CACHE_VERSION, "source": path.name,
                   "boxes": [box.__dict__ for box in boxes]}
        cache_file.write_text(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, indent=0),
                              encoding="utf-8")
    return boxes


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Warm the cache: python code/ocr.py dataset/evidence/images/*.png
    for arg in sys.argv[1:]:
        print(arg, len(ocr_image(arg)), flush=True)

import sys, collections as C
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1] + '/code')
import evidence
from data_loader import load_dataset
from identity import build_identity_index

skip_images = '--no-images' in sys.argv
if skip_images:
    evidence.EXTRACTORS['.png'] = lambda ef: ([], [])
ds = load_dataset()
ix = evidence.build_evidence_index(ds)
print('issues', ix.issues)
print('observations', len(ix.observations), 'coverage', len(ix.coverage))
print('by format/kind', sorted(C.Counter((o.source_format, o.kind) for o in ix.observations).items()))
print('states', sorted(C.Counter((o.source_format, o.state) for o in ix.observations).items(), key=str))
print('no system', C.Counter(o.source_format for o in ix.observations if o.resource_id and not o.system_id))
mism = [(o.evidence_id, o.resource_id, o.system_id) for o in ix.observations
        if o.resource_id and o.system_id and evidence.system_for_resource(o.resource_id) not in (None, o.system_id)]
print('system mismatch', len(mism), mism[:10])
print('unknown resource prefix', C.Counter(o.resource_id.rsplit('_', 1)[0] for o in ix.observations if o.resource_id and not evidence.system_for_resource(o.resource_id)))
print('observed>captured', sum(o.observed_at > o.captured_at for o in ix.observations))
idx = build_identity_index(ds)
users = C.Counter()
for o in ix.observations:
    for k, v in o.all_identifiers:
        if k == 'user': users['known' if v in {u.lower() for u in idx.identities} else 'unknown'] += 1
print('user refs', users)
emails = C.Counter()
known = {p.normalized for i in idx.identities.values() for p in i.periods if p.field == 'email'}
for o in ix.observations:
    for k, v in o.all_identifiers:
        if k == 'email': emails['known' if v in known else 'unknown'] += 1
print('email refs', emails)
for fid in sys.argv[2:]:
    if fid.startswith('--'): continue
    for o in ix.observations:
        if o.evidence_id == fid:
            print(' ', o.location, o.system_id, o.resource_id, o.kind, o.state, o.observed_at.isoformat(), sorted(o.identifiers), sorted(o.context_identifiers), sorted(o.linked_resources))
# case coverage: how many requests have >=1 matching observation available at audit_at
hit = C.Counter()
for t in ('requests', 'sample_requests'):
    for r in ds[t].rows:
        res = idx.resolve('email', r['email'], r['requested_at'])
        keys = evidence.identity_keys(idx[res.user_id])
        n = len(ix.resources_for(keys, r['audit_at']))
        hit[(t, 'none' if n == 0 else '1-3' if n <= 3 else '4+')] += 1
print('resources per case', sorted(hit.items()))

import sys, collections as C
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1] + '/code')
import evidence
from data_loader import load_dataset
from identity import build_identity_index

skip_images = '--no-images' in sys.argv
if skip_images:
    evidence.EXTRACTORS['.png'] = lambda ef: ([], [])
ds = load_dataset()
ix = evidence.build_evidence_index(ds)
print('issues', ix.issues)
print('observations', len(ix.observations), 'coverage', len(ix.coverage))
print('by format/kind', sorted(C.Counter((o.source_format, o.kind) for o in ix.observations).items()))
print('states', sorted(C.Counter((o.source_format, o.state) for o in ix.observations).items(), key=str))
print('no system', C.Counter(o.source_format for o in ix.observations if o.resource_id and not o.system_id))
mism = [(o.evidence_id, o.resource_id, o.system_id) for o in ix.observations
        if o.resource_id and o.system_id and evidence.system_for_resource(o.resource_id) not in (None, o.system_id)]

    return EvidenceFile(file_id, path, "test", ts(captured))

    out = {}

The evidence index is built and all 46 tests pass. One thing conflicts with your "no new dependencies" instruction: before your message arrived, I had already run `pip install rapidocr_onnxruntime` into your global Python. The code treats it as optional: without it, screenshots are reported as unsupported and everything else runs. I can uninstall it if you prefer.

**Files changed**
- [code/evidence.py](code/evidence.py) (new): extracts each evidence file into per-resource sightings and builds the index. Each sighting keeps:
  - the citable evidence ID, file capture time and record time
  - system and resource ID
  - state, inferred from fields like `enabled`, `restore_allowed`, `result`, HTTP status, row counts and search hits
  - identifiers the record contains, kept separate from identifiers it was only looked up by
- The index offers exact normalized matching (`matching`, `resources_for`), filtered by audit time (`at=`), plus `history`, `latest` and `listings`.
  - Activity rows are included and citable by `activity_id`.
  - Names are never used as a matching key.
- [code/ocr.py](code/ocr.py) (new): optional OCR with a cache keyed on file hash under `.cache/ocr/`.
- [code/tests/test_evidence.py](code/tests/test_evidence.py) (new): 24 tests covering each format, decoys, malformed files and timestamps, plus a test that builds the index from the real dataset.
- [.gitignore](.gitignore) (new): ignores `__pycache__/`, `.cache/`, `.venv/` and `.env`.
- `log.txt`: this turn appended.

**Formats handled** (no filenames or case IDs hardcoded)
- **SQL:** primary and replica tables, including the JSON-in-a-column replica tables.
- **JSON:** walked recursively at any nesting depth.
- **Logs:** six line formats, with lines joined by trace ID.
- **Text and PDF:** pipe-delimited rows become claims; PDFs are read with PyMuPDF.
- **Screenshots:** OCR text is grouped into visual rows, so a resource ID and an email on the same row are linked.

**Test results**
- 46 passed: 15 loader, 7 identity, 24 evidence.
- The tests caught four real bugs, all fixed:
  - resource IDs matched with trailing letters (`search_12x`)
  - pipe-row text hid the lookup subject
  - integrity-seal hashes were read as email hashes
  - an empty but valid SQL listing (`evidence_90`) was reported as an error
- Full corpus build: 0 issues, all 94 files extracted, 7,276 sightings and 361 snapshot listings.
  - Every sighting with a resource ID has a system.
  - No record time is later than its file's capture time.
- 12 of the 518 eval requests have no evidence citable at their `audit_at`.

**Unsupported formats**
- No format is unsupported while OCR is installed. Without it, the 11 PNG screenshots are skipped and listed in `index.unsupported`. That is the expected state on a clean machine, because OCR isn't in a requirements file yet.

- Screenshots and PDFs give links between identifiers and resources, but no record state; whoever uses the index decides what those mean.

import sys, collections as C
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1] + '/code')
import evidence
from data_loader import load_dataset
from identity import build_identity_index

ds = load_dataset()
idx = build_identity_index(ds)
ix = evidence.build_evidence_index(ds)
gold = {r['case_id']: r for r in ds['sample_output'].rows}
only = set(sys.argv[2:])
for req in ds['sample_requests'].rows:
    cid = req['case_id']
    if only and cid not in only:
        continue
    res = idx.resolve('email', req['email'], req['requested_at'])
    keys = evidence.identity_keys(idx[res.user_id])
    at = req['audit_at']
    g = gold[cid]
    print('=' * 100)
    print(cid, req['email'], res.user_id, res.reason, 'req', req['requested_at'].date(), 'audit', at, req['reported_status'], '->', g['deletion_status'])
    print('  TEXT:', req['request_text'][:150])
    for s in g['steps_json']:
        print('  GOLD', s['step_no'], s['phase'][:5], s['system_id'], s['resource_id'], s['operation'], s['evidence_id'])
    gold_res = {s['resource_id'] for s in g['steps_json']}
    rids = ix.resources_for(keys, at)
    allr = ix.resources_for(keys)
    for rid in sorted(rids | gold_res | (allr - rids)):
        tag = ('G' if rid in gold_res else '-') + ('A' if rid in rids else ('L' if rid in allr else '-'))
        hist = ix.history(rid)
        print(f'  [{tag}] {rid}')
        for o in hist:
            avail = 'ok ' if o.available_at(at) else 'LATE'
            own = sorted(v for k, v in o.identifiers if k in evidence.STRONG_KINDS)
            ctx = sorted(v for k, v in o.context_identifiers if k in evidence.STRONG_KINDS)
            mine = 'ME' if (o.all_identifiers & keys) else ('--' if o.all_identifiers else '  ')
            extra = o.attributes.get('event_type') or o.attributes.get('event') or o.attributes.get('record_type') or ''
            res_ = o.attributes.get('reported_result', '')
            print(f'      {avail} {mine} {o.observed_at:%m-%d %H:%M} {o.evidence_id:<13} {o.source_format:<8} {o.kind:<8} {str(o.state):<10} {o.location[:40]:<40} {extra} {res_} own={own} ctx={ctx}')

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1] + '/code')
from data_loader import load_dataset

ds = load_dataset(names=('sample_requests', 'sample_output', 'activity', 'requests'))
acts = sorted((a for a in ds['activity'].rows if a['event_type'] == 'DELETE_RECORD'
               and a['source_system'] == 'deletion_worker' and a['resource_id'].startswith('account_')),
              key=lambda a: a['event_time'])
gold = {r['case_id']: {s['resource_id'] for s in r['steps_json'] if s['resource_id'].startswith('account_')}
        for r in ds['sample_output'].rows}
print('account delete events', len(acts), 'requests', len(ds['requests'].rows) + len(ds['sample_requests'].rows))
for req in ds['sample_requests'].rows:
    g = gold[req['case_id']]
    after = [a for a in acts if a['event_time'] >= req['requested_at']]
    rank = next((i for i, a in enumerate(after) if a['resource_id'] in g), None)
    ga = [a for a in acts if a['resource_id'] in g]
    delay = [(a['event_time'] - req['requested_at']).total_seconds() / 3600 for a in ga]
    rdelay = [(a['event_time'] - req['reported_at']).total_seconds() / 3600 for a in ga]
    print(req['case_id'], sorted(g), 'rank', rank, 'hrs after req', [round(d, 2) for d in delay], 'hrs vs reported', [round(d, 2) for d in rdelay], 'details', [a['details'][:60] for a in ga])

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1] + '/code')
from data_loader import load_dataset

ds = load_dataset(names=('sample_requests', 'sample_output', 'activity', 'requests'))
acts = sorted((a for a in ds['activity'].rows if a['event_type'] == 'DELETE_RECORD'
               and a['source_system'] == 'deletion_worker' and a['resource_id'].startswith('account_')),
              key=lambda a: a['event_time'])
gold = {r['case_id']: {s['resource_id'] for s in r['steps_json'] if s['resource_id'].startswith('account_')}
        for r in ds['sample_output'].rows}
print('account delete events', len(acts), 'requests', len(ds['requests'].rows) + len(ds['sample_requests'].rows))
for req in ds['sample_requests'].rows:
    g = gold[req['case_id']]
    after = [a for a in acts if a['event_time'] >= req['requested_at']]
    rank = next((i for i, a in enumerate(after) if a['resource_id'] in g), None)
    ga = [a for a in acts if a['resource_id'] in g]
    delay = [(a['event_time'] - req['requested_at']).total_seconds() / 3600 for a in ga]
    rdelay = [(a['event_time'] - req['reported_at']).total_seconds() / 3600 for a in ga]
    print(req['case_id'], sorted(g), 'rank', rank, 'hrs after req', [round(d, 2) for d in delay], 'hrs vs reported', [round(d, 2) for d in rdelay], 'details', [a['details'][:60] for a in ga])

"""Decide whether a request_text authorizes deletion.

Deterministic, multilingual rules (no model calls). A request is treated as
non-deletion when it asks for another action (access, export, correction,
marketing opt-out, login help) or explicitly says the account must be kept;
those signals win over incidental deletion vocabulary such as "without
removing". Otherwise it is a deletion request when it contains deletion
vocabulary in any supported language.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

_NEGATED_DELETION = (
    r"\b(?:not|n't|never|without|no)\b[\w\s,'-]{0,40}?"
    r"\b(?:delet\w*|eras\w*|remov\w*|clos\w*|cancel\w*)"
)
NON_DELETION_PATTERNS = [
    _NEGATED_DELETION,
    r"\bdo(?:n't| not)\s+(?:delete|erase|remove|close|change)\b",
    r"\bkeep (?:the|my) (?:account|profile)\b",
    r"\bleave (?:the|my) (?:account|profile)\b",
    r"\b(?:account|profile)\b[\w\s]{0,30}\b(?:active|in place|as it is)\b",
    r"\bcontinue using\b",
    r"\bstill (?:use|need|want)\b",
    r"\bmarketing (?:lists?|emails?)\s+only\b",
    r"\b(?:stop|unsubscribe)\b[\w\s]{0,20}\b(?:promotional|marketing|newsletter)",
    r"\bcopy of (?:the|my|last)\b",
    r"\bdownload my\b",
    r"\bportable format\b",
    r"\binformation request\b",
    r"\bwhat personal (?:information|data) you hold\b",
    r"\b(?:correct|update|replace|change)\b[\w\s]{0,25}\b(?:name|surname|email address|phone|mobile|number)\b",
    r"\bmisspelled\b",
    r"\breset(?:ting)? (?:the |my )?(?:login|password)\b",
]
DELETION_PATTERNS = [
    r"\bdelet\w*", r"\beras\w*", r"\bremov\w*", r"\bclose (?:my|this|the) account\b",
    r"\bclos\w* (?:my|this|the) account\b", r"\bpermanently\b",
    r"\bl[öo]sch\w*", r"\bsuppression\b", r"\bsupprim\w*", r"\beffac\w*",
    r"\beliminaci[óo]n\b", r"\belimin\w*", r"\bborr\w*", r"\bexclus[ãa]o\b", r"\bexclu\w*",
    r"\bapag\w*", r"\bcancel\w*", r"\busu[ńn]\w*", r"\bverwijder\w*", r"\bcancell\w*",
    r"削除", r"删除", r"刪除", r"삭제", r"удал\w*", r"видал\w*",
]
_NON_DELETION = [re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE) for p in NON_DELETION_PATTERNS]
_DELETION = [re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE) for p in DELETION_PATTERNS]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Intent:
    authorizes_deletion: bool
    reason: str


def classify_request(text: str) -> Intent:
    normalized = text.replace("’", "'")
    for pattern in _NON_DELETION:
        if m := pattern.search(normalized):
            return Intent(False, f"non-deletion signal: {m.group(0)!r}")
    for pattern in _DELETION:
        if m := pattern.search(normalized):
            return Intent(True, f"deletion signal: {m.group(0)!r}")
    return Intent(False, "no deletion signal")

"""Ghost Data Still Exists - deletion audit agent.

Usage:
    python code/main.py                      # audit dataset/deletion_requests.csv -> output.csv
    python code/main.py --sample             # audit the sample requests -> sample_predictions.csv
    python code/main.py --output path.csv    # choose the output path
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from data_loader import DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR, REPO_ROOT, load_dataset  # noqa: E402
from engine import DeletionEngine  # noqa: E402
from identity import _natural_key  # noqa: E402
from planner import serialize_steps, validate_steps  # noqa: E402


def run(dataset_dir: Path, table: str, output: Path, verbose: bool = False) -> list:
    dataset = load_dataset(dataset_dir)
    if dataset.issues:
        print(f"warning: {len(dataset.issues)} dataset issues", file=sys.stderr)
    engine = DeletionEngine(dataset)
    for problem in engine.index.issues + engine.index.unsupported:
        print(f"evidence: {problem}", file=sys.stderr)

    results = []
    for request in sorted(dataset[table].rows, key=lambda r: _natural_key(r["case_id"])):
        result = engine.decide(request)
        validate_steps(result.deletion_status, result.steps)
        results.append(result)
        if verbose:
            print(result.case_id, result.deletion_status, len(result.steps), result.user_id)
            for note in result.notes:
                print("   ", note)

    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with output.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
        writer = csv.writer(handle, lineterminator="\n")
        writer.writerow(["case_id", "deletion_status", "steps_json"])
        for result in results:
            writer.writerow([result.case_id, result.deletion_status, serialize_steps(result.steps)])
    print(f"wrote {len(results)} rows to {output}")
    return results


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--dataset", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR)
    parser.add_argument("--sample", action="store_true", help="audit sample requests instead")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    table = "sample_requests" if args.sample else "requests"
    default = REPO_ROOT / ("sample_predictions.csv" if args.sample else "output.csv")
    run(args.dataset, table, args.output or default, args.verbose)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

from identity import _natural_key  # noqa: E402
from planner import serialize_steps, validate_steps  # noqa: E402


def run(dataset_dir: Path, table: str, output: Path, verbose: bool = False) -> list:
    dataset = load_dataset(dataset_dir)
    if dataset.issues:
        print(f"warning: {len(dataset.issues)} dataset issues", file=sys.stderr)
    engine = DeletionEngine(dataset)
    for problem in engine.index.issues + engine.index.unsupported:
        print(f"evidence: {problem}", file=sys.stderr)

    results = []
    for request in sorted(dataset[table].rows, key=lambda r: _natural_key(r["case_id"])):
        result = engine.decide(request)
        validate_steps(result.deletion_status, result.steps)
        results.append(result)
        if verbose:
            print(result.case_id, result.deletion_status, len(result.steps), result.user_id)
            for note in result.notes:
                print("   ", note)

    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with output.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
        writer = csv.writer(handle, lineterminator="\n")
        writer.writerow(["case_id", "deletion_status", "steps_json"])
        for result in results:
            writer.writerow([result.case_id, result.deletion_status, serialize_steps(result.steps)])
    print(f"wrote {len(results)} rows to {output}")

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--dataset", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR)
    parser.add_argument("--sample", action="store_true", help="audit sample requests instead")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    table = "sample_requests" if args.sample else "requests"
    default = REPO_ROOT / ("sample_predictions.csv" if args.sample else "output.csv")
    run(args.dataset, table, args.output or default, args.verbose)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Score predictions against labelled answers (e.g. the public sample_output.csv).

    python code/evaluation/main.py --predictions sample_predictions.csv \
        --gold dataset/sample_output.csv

Metrics:
* status accuracy   - deletion_status matches;
* step precision / recall / F1 - steps matched on (phase, operation, state,
  system_id, resource_id, evidence_id);
* field accuracy    - per-field agreement over position-aligned steps;
* sequence accuracy - cases whose full steps_json equals the gold exactly.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

FIELDS = ("phase", "system_id", "resource_id", "operation", "state", "evidence_id")


def load(path: Path) -> dict[str, tuple[str, list[dict]]]:
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
        return {row["case_id"]: (row["deletion_status"], json.loads(row["steps_json"]))
                for row in csv.DictReader(handle)}


def key(step: dict) -> tuple:
    return tuple(step[f] for f in FIELDS)


def score(predicted: dict, gold: dict) -> dict:
    status_ok = tp = fp = fn = exact = 0
    field_hits: Counter = Counter()
    aligned = 0
    failures = []
    for case_id, (gold_status, gold_steps) in sorted(gold.items()):
        pred_status, pred_steps = predicted.get(case_id, ("MISSING", []))
        status_ok += pred_status == gold_status
        g, p = Counter(map(key, gold_steps)), Counter(map(key, pred_steps))
        hit = sum((g & p).values())
        tp, fp, fn = tp + hit, fp + sum(p.values()) - hit, fn + sum(g.values()) - hit
        for gs, ps in zip(gold_steps, pred_steps):
            aligned += 1
            for f in FIELDS:
                field_hits[f] += gs[f] == ps[f]
        aligned_extra = abs(len(gold_steps) - len(pred_steps))
        aligned += aligned_extra
        same = pred_status == gold_status and [key(s) for s in pred_steps] == [key(s) for s in gold_steps]
        exact += same
        if not same:
            failures.append((case_id, gold_status, pred_status,
                             sorted(set(g) - set(p)), sorted(set(p) - set(g))))
    n = len(gold)
    precision = tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else 0.0
    recall = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else 0.0
    return {
        "cases": n,
        "status_accuracy": status_ok / n if n else 0.0,
        "step_precision": precision,
        "step_recall": recall,
        "step_f1": 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall) if precision + recall else 0.0,
        "field_accuracy": {f: field_hits[f] / aligned if aligned else 0.0 for f in FIELDS},
        "sequence_accuracy": exact / n if n else 0.0,
        "failures": failures,
    }


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--predictions", type=Path, default=root / "sample_predictions.csv")
    parser.add_argument("--gold", type=Path, default=root / "dataset" / "sample_output.csv")
    parser.add_argument("--failures", action="store_true", help="print per-case differences")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    result = score(load(args.predictions), load(args.gold))
    print(f"cases: {result['cases']}")
    print(f"status accuracy:   {result['status_accuracy']:.3f}")
    print(f"step precision:    {result['step_precision']:.3f}")
    print(f"step recall:       {result['step_recall']:.3f}")
    print(f"step F1:           {result['step_f1']:.3f}")
    print("field accuracy:    " + ", ".join(f"{k}={v:.3f}" for k, v in result["field_accuracy"].items()))
    print(f"sequence accuracy: {result['sequence_accuracy']:.3f}")
    if args.failures:
        for case_id, gs, ps, missing, extra in result["failures"]:
            print(f"\n{case_id}: gold={gs} predicted={ps}")
            for s in missing:
                print("   missing", s)
            for s in extra:
                print("   extra  ", s)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
